utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour, please proceed and please keep in mind that while reading the speed of speech often goes up.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: The accused are charged with approximately 20 murders committed by Arkan's Men during the Zvornik attack. And I refer the Chamber to the confidential evidence table at E8 and the evidence of JF-070. Following Zvornik's take-over, the Zvornik TO under command of Branko Popovic, also known as Marko Pavlovic, continued to persecute non-Serbs. Pavlovic was closely associated with the Serbian DB and carried out their bidding. He came to Zvornik with Kostic, the same Kostic upon whose statue Stanisic placed a wreath in the Kula video, which is P61. Pavlovic referred to Kostic as boss. On the confidential evidence table, this is E9. Locals in Zvornik municipality knew Pavlovic to be Serbian DB sent from Belgrade to "fix the situation" or "control things" in Zvornik. Those quotes are at E10 and E11 on the confidential evidence table. Pavlovic had frequent contact with Stanisic's assistant, Tepavcevic, and local members of and affiliates of the Serbian DB based just across the river from Zvornik. Sources for this are at E12 and E13 on the confidential evidence table. In a subordinate's application to the Captain Dragan fund, which Simatovic presented at the Red Berets' award ceremony as one of the Serbian DB unit's humanitarian activities, Pavlovic was listed as being the commander of a special military police unit. And I refer Your Honours to slide 54. Through his close connections to Kostic and the JNA, Pavlovic procured weapons for the Zvornik TO from Croatia and Serbia. As evidence that this was part of the common plan, Mladic's military notebook reflects that Pavlovic reported at a meeting with Karadzic and Mladic on 30 June 1992, that co-operation with the army remained firm including for the purpose of supply. And this is from P2528, page 8. As TO commander, Marko Pavlovic co-ordinated all of the armed forces and paramilitaries operating in Zvornik. He approved payroll sheets authorising the Zvornik interim government to pay the various paramilitary groups and JNA members under the Zvornik TO. I refer Your Honours to slide 55 for the relevant exhibits. In the months following Zvornik's take-over, Serb forces continued to persecute the Muslim civilian population through arbitrary detentions, beatings, and other acts. In this context, half of the Bosniak village of Kozluk's predominantly Muslim population had fled Kozluk by June 1992. The Serb forces under Pavlovic's TO thus succeeded in forcibly displacing the non-Serb population by creating the same environment of fear that Serb forces employed in the Krajina and the SBWS. In June, more than 20.000 Serb refugees came to Zvornik. In order to implement the common plan and also to house Serb refugees, Serb forces rounded up 1800 Muslim civilians from Kozluk and the neighbouring Skocic and loaded them on to buses organised by the local Serb leadership. Pavlovic signed deportation orders which are P2138 and P2139. The Bosnian Serb police transported the refugees under armed guard over the Bosnian border into Serbia and the Serbian police guarded their transport through Serbia to the Hungarian border. There the Serbian MUP supplied the convoy with passports to enter Hungary, as is clear from the MUP stamp on the passports at P2141. The Serbian MUP contributed enormously to this elaborate forcible deportation process, from allowing the initial crossing of 1800 people over Serbia's border to co-ordinating local Serbian police to guard and transport the convoy through the entire length of the Serbian territory, to finally issuing hundreds of passports. I refer the Chamber to the evidence on the confidential evidence table at E14 and E15 regarding crimes in Zvornik municipality after the take-over, including these mass deportations. In his notebook, Mladic states that at a meeting on 30 June 1992, among Mladic, Karadzic, and representatives of several municipalities, the president of SDS Zvornik stated that: "We have successfully implemented the president's decision to settle Divic and Kozluk with our children." And this is P2528, pages 4 to 5. Marko Pavlovic then stated: "We are most active in evicting the Muslims, we brought peace to Sepak, Divic, and Kozluk. Some of them wanted to move out, while we demanded it. We had to evict some of the people also for the sake of our 'heroes' who fled from Kovacevici." And this is the same document at pages 8 through 9. With the Muslim population of Zvornik drastically reduced through murders, forcible transfer and deportation, and persecution of ethnic Bosniaks, Pavlovic went on to report at this meeting that in Zvornik Arkan and Seselj's volunteer formations had "enjoyed exceptional success." And this is page 7 of that exhibit. A Serbian DB document from July 1992 characterised the situation in Zvornik as "genocide committed in the Zvornik region by the SDG volunteers and the volunteers from Loznica." This is on the confidential evidence table at E16. The fact that Pavlovic reported to Mladic and Karadzic, two JCE members, about the successful contributions of two other JCE members to operations that a DB operative termed genocide, indicates that the large-scale killing and forcible displacement of non-Serb civilians in Zvornik and Bijeljina had intentionally targeted non-Serbs exactly as the JCE members had envisioned. As with the Zvornik-Bijeljina operation, the Prosecution's case is that Stanisic and Simatovic planned the Bosanski Samac operation. Through the Serbian DB, they trained and armed local Serbs at the Ilok/Pajzos training camp. Simatovic then personally ordered this Red Beret unit to attack Bosanski Samac where they murdered, forcibly transferred, deported and otherwise persecuted the municipality's non-Serb population, in co-ordination with other Serb forces such as the JNA and local TO. Prior to the take-over, ethnic tensions were rising in Bosanski Samac, as local Serb leadership made a number of policy decisions that discriminated against non-Serbs, as indicated on slide 59. In late March 1992, a Serbian DB training camp near Ilok called Pajzos in Eastern Slavonia, which Ms. Friedman briefly discussed, began training recruits from Bosanski Samac. The camp's instructors were members of the Serbian DB, most notably, Dragan Djordjevic, also known as Crni, Srecko Radovanovic, also known as Debeli, and Slobodan Miljkovic, also known as Lugar. Crni's membership in the Serbian DB is well established, in the evidence of Todorovic and JF-047. Todorovic, chief of the Bosanski Samac police, recounted an incident from the summer of 1992 that exemplified the close relationship between Crni and both accused. Crni was arrested. He asked Todorovic to talk to "his people" about getting him released. Todorovic then went to the Serbian MUP in Belgrade in search of Simatovic, but was instead directed to Stanisic. Upon learning of Crni's arrest, Stanisic said that those responsible had "touched into a hornet's nest." And he would tell them to release Crni immediately. Sure enough, Crni was released some ten days later. This is from P1576 at pages 23475 through 77. In addition, there's evidence that Crni joined the unit on 5 October 1991, that Stanisic was personally involved in recruiting him, and that the Serbian DB was aware that Crni, like many other DB recruits, had previously engaged in criminal activities. Please refer to the confidential evidence table at E17 for this evidence. JF-047 and Todorovic have testified that Debeli and Lugar were also members of the Serbian DB subordinate to Crni. A request for assistance that Lugar later wrote to the Serbian DB outlines his involvement in the DB, training at the Lezimir and Ilok/Pajzos camps, then commanding a unit in the Bosanski Samac attack, and this is P1425. The collaboration that resulted in the Ilok/Pajzos camp becoming involved in Bosanski Samac is itself evidence of the JCE. Police and Defence at the local and Serbian levels devised the plan for the Serbian DB to train Bosanski Samac locals. Stevan Todorovic and Milos Bogdanovic, who as the municipal secretariat of national defence, met in Belgrade with a member of the federal Secretariat for National Defence and with Milan Prodanic of the Serbian DB. Prodanic later informed Milos Bogdanovic that he would send men to give training at a camp organised by the Serbian MUP. Together, Milos Bogdanovic and Todorovic recruited local men to undergo military training at Ilok/Pajzos in March 1992. This is from the evidence of Todorovic, and Lugar's statement, which is P1428 at page 4, corroborates Todorovic's involvement. The camp at Ilok/Pajzos was set up to train special purpose units of the Serbian MUP. These came to be commonly known in Bosanski Samac as the Red Berets or as the Grey Wolves, based on the recognisable grey wolf insignia on their sleeves. The non-Serb civilians whom they brutalised knew them as the Specials. As indicated on slide 61, the KDF applications of individuals who trained at Ilok/Pajzos during this time characterised the unit as either the Special Unit of the MUP of Serbia or as Grey Wolves. And these applications also demonstrate Debeli's and Lugar's role in the Bosanski Samac operations. According to JF-047, the Red Berets who were trained at Ilok/Pajzos in March 1992 knew Simatovic to be their commander. There is also evidence of Stanisic's superiority to Simatovic and the Ilok/Pajzos Red Berets for which I refer the Chamber to the confidential evidence table at E18. Ilok/Pajzos, like the other Serbian DB camps that my colleagues have discussed, was among the training camps that Simatovic himself highlighted during the Red Beret's award ceremony in 1997. One former Red Beret provided detailed evidence of the DB training camp at Ilok/Pajzos, including the role of Simatovic, Bozovic, Dragoslav Krsmanovic, Zvezdan Jovanovic, and Arkan. And I refer the Chamber to P523, pages 7 through 11 and to E19 on the confidential evidence table. Just before the take-over, Simatovic personally instructed the Red Berets at the Ilok/Pajzos camp on the plan and objective of the upcoming operation. Fifty Red Berets including Crni, Debeli, and Lugar, 30 men from Serbia and 20 local trainees arrived by helicopter in Batkusa on 11 April 1992. On the night between 16 and 17 April, these Red Berets, co-operating with the local police and TO, secured the key facilities in town. Once the Red Beret units secured the important structures, the JNA took over and JF-047 gives extensive evidence about Simatovic's briefing and the take-over. Two days before the take-over, Crni had attending a meeting with Todorovic, Blagoje Simic and others where they discussed including the Red Berets in the existing 17th Tactical Group of the JNA, which later became the VRS's 2nd Posavina Brigade. This is Todorovic's evidence P1576 at page 23452. During the Bosanski Samac operations, the Red Berets were in fact incorporated into TG-17. Lieutenant-Colonel Nikolic, commander of the TG-17, held overall tactical and operational command of the units participating in the take-over. This co-operation advanced the JCE's common purpose and reflected the shared intent among the JCE's members whose organisations were represented at this meeting. Namely, the Serbian DB, the JNA, the RS MUP, and Bosnian Serb political leadership. Nevertheless, the Red Berets functioned as a distinct unit. Temporary subordination to the JNA did not affect the Red Berets permanent chain of command. JF-047 testified that orders came from Crni through Debeli. The Red Berets' victims easily discerned that they were not JNA, but rather "attached to another command," said Tihic at transcript page 3215. The difference was apparent in their uniform, behaviour, training, Serbian regional dialect, and their "assertion of power." This evidence is also from Tihic at page 3219 to 20 in the transcript. Nikolic endorsed the Red Berets as "a legal elite unit of Serbian commandos, whose arrival had been legalized through the official organs of the government and the army, both at the level of Samac municipality and at the highest level in Serbia and Yugoslavia." This is from P1418, page 1. Nikolic's description reflects the Red Berets' central role in implementing the common criminal purpose and the shared intent of high level members of the JCE. As in other areas discussed today, the Serbian DB armed and equipped various Serb forces in Bosanski Samac and neighbouring areas. JF-047 testified that Vaso Mijovic, a known DB member, brought four to six truck-loads of ammunition from Belgrade to Brcko on an approximately weekly basis, giving a few cases to the small Red Berets unit and storing the rest in VRS hangars for VRS use. The Serbian MUP also lent equipment to the VRS's 2nd Posavina Brigade as evidenced by P1523. The Red Berets committed a string of atrocities targeting non-Serb civilians in the wake of the Bosanski Samac take-over, and I refer the Chamber to the evidence of witnesses Tihic, Lukac, JF-079 and JF-012. The accused are charged with the murders of at least 16 Muslim and Croat civilians at Crkvina on 7 May, 1992, after Lugar and several other Red Berets went on a shooting rampage. There's evidence that Lugar committed these murders on specific orders in the confidential evidence table at E20. For a full account of the Crkvina massacre, please see E21 and E22. The Red Berets co-ordinated numerous forced exchanges, transferring non-Serb civilians from Bosanski Samac to Croatia as shown on slide 64. The accused intended these crimes. They recruited Red Berets with criminal inclinations, then planned and ordered the operation which went exactly as intended. As Tihic testified, "Special units that took part in the attack against Bosanski Samac, or who led the attack against Bosanski Samac, were the masters. I know full well that nothing could have been decided without them afterwards. You could see straightaway that these were persons who were prone to crime and that killing someone meant nothing to them." This is from page 3120. Tihic went on to state that "Crni was the commander of all. He is the one who issued orders." This is 3136 in the transcript. A report of the 2nd Posavina Brigade of the Bosanski Samac operations described the Red Berets "official role as war criminals in the area." And went on to report that "criminals of a Yugoslav calibre were hiding among the Serbian commandos who had come to train the Serbian police. With the blessing of those who had brought them in and those who had sent them, they engaged in unheard of looting of private and socially owned property. The massive arrests and isolation of Croats and Muslims followed without any criteria, and some of the prisoners were subjected to measures such as abuse, torture, or even killing." This is P1418, pages 1 to 2. The Doboj operation followed the same pattern as in Bosanski Samac. The Prosecution's case is that it was planned and ordered by the accused and that it was committed through implementation of the JCE. As in Bosanski Samac, the Serbian DB trained and armed local Serbs at the Mount Ozren Red Berets training camp led by Bozovic, a prominent member of the Serbian DB. Through Bozovic, the accused ordered the Red Berets unit to attack Doboj where they murdered, forcibly transferred, deported, and otherwise persecuted the municipality's non-Serb population in co-ordination with other Serb forces including the JNA, local TO, and local police. Leading up to the take-over, the Serb leadership implemented a number of policies and laws to discriminate against the Bosniak and Croat population, indicated on slide 66. In early 1992, Bozovic, a member of the DB who Mr. Weber has already introduced, established a Red Berets training camp at Mount Ozren. According to JF-005, Simatovic visited the Mount Ozren camp and there's evidence that Stanisic ordered and approved weapon transfers from Serbia to the camp. Please see the confidential evidence table at E23. As with the Ilok/Pajzos camp, Simatovic referred to Mount Ozren at the Red Berets award ceremony on 4 May 1997. Bozovic was the commander of this camp and of the special units in Doboj. As one of the Serbian DB special unit's original members, he was directly subordinate to Stanisic and Simatovic. He was a prominent figure in the Serbian DB, as demonstrated by his introduction during the Red Berets award ceremony as one of "the unit's veteran officers." To which Milosevic responded that he had personally read Bozovic's reports and this is P61, page 4. E24 on the confidential evidence table has evidence that Mr. Stanisic was directly involved in recruiting Bozovic. Bozovic had a vicious reputation and Mladic considered him akin to mafia, having established "deaths camps" with Arkan. And this is from P2956. Following the same pattern seen in Bosanski Samac, the local Serb political and military leadership funneled local recruits to Mount Ozren through training. Together the president of the SDS Doboj Municipal Board Milan Ninkovic and JNA commander, Milovan Stankovic ensured that formations of the Doboj police, JNA and volunteers were sent for training. The recruits received camouflage uniforms and red berets with insignias stating JSN, Special Purpose Unit, with a brown wolf. They became known in Doboj as the Red Berets. On 3 May 1992, around 300 men in the Mount Ozren trained Red Berets unit, at Bozovic's order, took over Doboj by force. The Red Berets secured important structures to prevent Muslims from entering. They forced people found in the buildings to declare their loyalty to the Serbs, which is evidence of their persecutory intent. As in Bosanski Samac, and reflective of the joint nature of the JCE, the Red Berets co-ordinated the take-over with the JNA and Serb paramilitaries. Stankovic had overall command of the Doboj operation with Bozovic. There's evidence that Stankovic received orders from Stanisic through Bozovic. Please see the confidential evidence table at E25. Officially, the Red Berets were under CSB Doboj, but in fact they were under Bozovic, under the Serbian DB. CSB Doboj's payment records during that period, listed on slide 68, show that Bozovic's group was paid as a special group. Furthermore, several KDF applications, also on the slide, indicate that Mount Ozren trainees joined Red Beret units or MUP of Serbia units under the command of Bozovic and Frenki. In July 1992, many of the Red Berets were integrated into the military police. JF-005 testified that Stankovic, who by this point was TG Ozren's commander, continued co-ordinating with Bozovic. The Red Berets in the military police thus continued receiving orders from Bozovic. They were separated from their base unit and their commanders were not allowed to ask questions. During and following Doboj's take-over, the Red Berets pursued a campaign of violence and persecution targeting Doboj's Muslim and Croat population. Bozovic ordered his men to torture non-Serb civilians and the victims recognised him as being in control of the Red Berets. I refer Your Honours to the evidence of JF-008, JF-009, B-1115, Ahmetovic and Hadzovic for more details of this persecution and evidence of discriminatory intent. The accused are charged with at least 27 murders committed on 12 July 1992, after the Red Berets and other Serb forces used non-Serb detainees as a human shield against the Bosnian forces. And for this I refer Your Honours to the evidence of JF-008, JF-009, and Hadzovic, and P254 and P92. As a result of the horrific crimes in Doboj and reports of a similar pattern of attacks in other municipalities, thousands of Muslims and Croats fled their homes in Doboj and many others were detained and forcibly exchanged within Bosnia and across the Croatian border. And for this evidence, I refer the Chamber to the evidence of Hadzovic, JF-005, B-1115, JF-008, JF-009, and Exhibits P93, P94, and P1816. The Red Berets' Doboj operations followed the same pattern as in Bosanski Samac, entailed similar acts of violence, and achieved the same results, emptying these municipalities of non-Serbs. Having seen the Red Berets' success in Bosanski Samac, Stanisic and Simatovic, through their loyal subordinate Bozovic, repeated this pattern in Doboj because it furthered the JCE's purpose. Predictably, Doboj was just as successful. The "Doboj experience" was later described as "an example of how a Serbian state should be created." This is from P1435, page 3. I'll now turn the floor over to Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Slobodan Medic, aka Boca and the Skorpions were deployed to the Serbian front to the Trnovo front for approximately one months to the end of June to the end of July 1995. During their deployment to the Trnovo area, they were engaged in operations in co-ordination with the VRS and RS MUP forces. This coordination culminated in the execution of six Bosnian Muslim men and boys who had been captured in part of the attack by Serb forces on Srebrenica. Evidence has been adduced showing that the Skorpions had been in Djeletovci in SBWS since the end of 1991, or the beginning of 1992. Djeletovci is located near other locations central to JCE operations throughout the indictment period, including Tovarnik, Njemci, which is near Ziriste and Ilok/Pajzos. I refer the Chamber to the evidence of JF-032, JF-024, JF-048, and Borivoje Savic. Three co-ordinated operations in Bosnia in 1995 demonstrate the implementation of the common criminal plan: Pauk, Trnovo, and Sanski Most. At the end of 1994, the Skorpions under Slobodan Medic were deployed to joint field operations in conjunction with other Serb forces in the Velika Kladusa Pauk operation. For additional evidence in relation to the Pauk operation, I refer the Chamber to P2146 and P235. The Pauk Joint Command in which the Skorpions and Arkan's SDG operated continued into May 1995. At the same time, the accused not only sent troops and support for Pauk, they were also present themselves with great regularity in Bosnia in May to June 1995. Within ten days following the release of the last UN hostages, the Serbian MUP deployed their forces to join in operations at the Trnovo front in conjunction with the very same Bosnian Serb MUP and VRS forces who had been engaged at Pauk, who had taken UN troops hostage, and who at the time of deployment were preparing to take over Srebrenica. The Serbian MUP forces including the Skorpions and Arkan's Tigers engaged in operations at the Trnovo front throughout the month of July 1995, during which time the Skorpions executed the six men and boys. Following the pullout order conveyed by Vaso Mijovic, a DB agent, Serbian MUP forces pulled out were the Trnovo front on the 24th of July, 1995. Six weeks later, Arkan's Men were deployed to Sanski Most to carry out operations there. The proximity in time and the centralised co-ordination involved in Pauk, Trnovo, and Sanski Most characterise the last phase of the implementation of the common criminal plan. The Skorpions and Arkan's Men had been deployed to participate in the Pauk operation, Mr. Stanisic said on the 6th of April, 1995, "I sent 150 men from Slavonija through Pauk. The crossing had to be done quietly." You can see this excerpt on slide 71. At a meeting on the 30th of June, 1995 in Belgrade at which Mladic, Milosevic, and Stanisic were talking with Fikret Abdic, Stanisic is recorded as saying, "We have been supplying 100.000 men for six months. There is poor organisation in RS, they plundered us." Milosevic suggested, "Jovica should resolve logistics problems, and let RS resolve this problem of holding up convoys." Mr. Stanisic stated, "I can find 120 perfect men who would come there in seven days. They would be from the eastern sector. That is support. They should not be engaged (we gave 80 from Erdut, we gave 80 from Djeletovci)." I refer the Chamber to the Pauk diary admitted at P235 and to P2149. It should be noted that in the Pauk diary which spans from November 1994 through to the end of May 1995, Jovica Stanisic is named explicitly twice; Frenki, 15 times; Legija, 78 times; Bozovic, 37 times; and Kobac, Rajo Bozovic's nickname, appears at least 120 times. The Prosecution evidence has demonstrated that the deployment of the Skorpions to Trnovo to assist in carrying out the Eastern Bosnia portion of the common criminal plan was designed in the course of two meetings which took place prior to that deployment and which were attended by high-level DB officials and other central actors in the plan. May I request private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Following that first meeting, there was a second meeting which took place in the building of the Serbian MUP in Belgrade before the Skorpions left for Trnovo. This meeting was attended by individuals central to Serbian MUP and DB hierarchy including Ilija Kojic, who worked directly for Mr. Stanisic, as Ms. Friedman has already discussed. Also attending this meeting were Milan Milanovic aka Mrgud, Ljubo Miljevic, Arkan, Slobodan Medic aka Boca, Radovan Stojicic aka Badza, and several others. P1666, an excerpt of which appears on slide 74, describes this meeting including the location and the attendees. Mr. Bakrac discussed this meeting in his submissions. For corroboration, I refer the Chamber to the confidential evidence table at F1. At this meeting, according to the evidence led in this case, Badza told those present that the RS was being attacked and that if possible Arkan's unit, the Skorpions, and the Plavi unit should help the VRS in Trnovo for a month. I refer the Chamber to the confidential evidence table at F2. Witness evidence confirmed that Frenki had arranged for the Tigers to take part in the Treskavica operation. I refer the Chamber to the confidential evidence table at F3 and F4. Ilija Kojic's role was to organise deployment of these three units that made up the battalion sent to the war front in Trnovo. Please refer to the confidential evidence table at F5. Witnesses testified that Mrgud was the intermediary between Slobodan Medic and Milorad Ulemek, aka Legija, and the DB leadership in Belgrade. One witness reported that Slobodan Medic himself had boasted that his orders came from Stanisic and Simatovic. Dejan Sliskovic testified that Slobodan Medic commanded the Skorpions and during combat activities he was subordinated to the Red Beret command staff. Simatovic visited the Skorpion headquarters in Djeletovci after the events in Trnovo. I refer the Chamber to the confidential evidence table at F6. The Skorpions deployed to the Trnovo front at the end of June 1995. According to his own notes, Mladic was at Jahorina on the 25th of May, 1995. I refer the Chamber to P394. On the 23rd of June, 1995, Mladic said in a meeting with Karadzic and others: "We must conduct an operation near Trnovo." On the 30th of June, 1995, the Serbian MUP's anti-terrorist unit sent a telegram to Ratko Mladic and in response Mladic issued this urgent order, P1454. Mladic ordered on the 1st of July that helicopters be provided for the evacuation of any men wounded at the Trnovo front and that any such injuries be reported formally. Serbian MUP hierarchy was informed of this. This pattern of documentation suggests that the Serbian MUP were providing their pilots and possibly their helicopters for the purpose of assisting in the evacuation of wounded fighters at the Trnovo front. Serb forces on the ground issued regular reports which appear on slide 77. These official military and police reports providing information on the wounded including Serbian MUP members span throughout July 1995. For additional corroboration, I refer the Chamber to the transcript at 10059. The Prosecution case that the Skorpions as a unit of the Serbian MUP were deployed to the Trnovo front where they were subordinated to or operated in co-ordination with other Serb forces, in this case, including Arkan's Men, the RS MUP, and VRS forces. The accused used their authority to direct and organise the financing, logistical support, or other substantial assistance or support to these special units and continued to send forces and provide support to the Serbian MUP forces on the ground at the Trnovo front over an extended period of time before, during, and after the large-scale massacres at Srebrenica and Zepa and the consequent execution of the Trnovo victims. Evidence of the arming and provision of supplies and logistical support to the Skorpions by the Serbian MUP was presented by JF-048 who testified that the Skorpions came to the DB camp in Pajzos to obtain ammunition from the warehouse. The DB provided multiple licence plates to the Skorpions for ease of movement, several different uniforms, Serbian MUP badges once they deployed to Trnovo, higher salaries than other police work, according to one estimate higher by a multiple of seven, payment in newly printed dinars, training, communication via radio and telephone with Arkan's unit and with VRS forces during the operation. For additional evidence of the contributions by the accused, I refer the Chamber to the confidential evidence table at F7 and to slide number 78. In addition to the pattern of reports on the wounded, the Prosecution has presented a pattern of official police and military reports from the front describing the day-to-day activities in and around the Trnovo front involving the Skorpions/Serbian MUP forces throughout July 1995. The documents are listed on slides 79 and 80. P1452 dated the 1st of July, 1995, "Activities commenced the previous day were continued at the Trnovo battle-field on the 30th of June 1995. The combat group was described as including the Skorpions Serbian MUP." P1455 from the 3rd of July and P1458 from the 7th of July further described the joint operations of the MUP forces of the RS, Serbia and RSK along with the VRS at the Trnovo front. P1459, the 7th of July lists the numerical strength of the police engaged at the Trnovo front including "the Republic of Serbia and the Republic of Serbian Krajina special unit 350 policemen." By the 10th of July 1995, the reports describe the advance of the forces at Srebrenica. On that same day, as further evidence of the co-ordination on the ground as a broader part of the Srebrenica offensive, Mladic issued P1462, a dispatch appearing before you, to all SDBs and all police stations on behalf of the "supreme commander of the Republika Srpska Armed Forces and in order to crush the enemy offensive from the Srebrenica protected zone." He ordered the singling out of a mixed company of joint MUP forces of the RSK, Serbia, and Republika Srpska to send to the Srebrenica sector on the 11th of July, 1995. We know that Vaso Mijovic was a person in a leadership role in the DB during the Trnovo campaign. I refer the Chamber to the confidential evidence table at F8. The Prosecution has presented a compelling body of evidence demonstrating the deployment of the Skorpions to Trnovo by the end of July 1995. The co-operation and co-ordination amongst these forces throughout the month of July 1995 and concluding with the Skorpions being pulled out at the end of July 1995. Operations at the Trnovo front are a perfect example of the type of joint operations which epitomised the way the JCE functioned. In addition to deploying their forces, the evidence demonstrates that the accused went themselves to the region. During the end of May and until the middle of June 1995, Stanisic and Simatovic were in Bosnia during the negotiations for the release of the UN hostages. Throughout this time, as stated by Stanisic himself, the accused were both in direct contact with the highest level Serb and Bosnian Serb authorities including Slobodan Milosevic, Radovan Karadzic, and Ratko Mladic, all JCE members. The Prosecution refers the Chamber to Exhibits P48.17, D142, transcript at page T-430 to 433. We also refer the Chamber to the transcript at page 2064 to 2067. The accused contributed forces and their personal presence, as well as other extensive logistical and operational support to the VRS and RS MUP forces on the ground in Pauk, then in Trnovo, and finally in Sanski Most. The Skorpions, as a unit of the Serbian MUP, provided the ultimate participation in their acts in furtherance of the common criminal plan, the execution of six men and boys captured from Srebrenica. Vaso Mijovic, a DB official, informed the Skorpions that they had been ordered to pull out of Trnovo and within a few days after that order, Milan Milanovic, aka Mrgud travelled to Trnovo to retrieve the DB forces from the field. Six weeks later, the DB deployed Arkan's Men to Sanski Most, as part of the co-ordinated widespread and systematic attack against the non-Serb civilian population. On the 16th of April, 1992, Sanski Most was attacked by Serb forces. Ultimately those non-Serbs who did not flee due to the killings and other acts of violence were forced to leave due to the coercive and oppressive environment. Those who remained until 1995 endured continual discriminatory treatment. I refer the Chamber to the transcript at page 3028. The Sasina and Trnovo village executions were part of this widespread and systematic attack upon the non-Serb civilian population in Sanski Most and bore a nexus to the armed conflict. Arkan and his men, as explained by my colleagues, were an effective choice for the carrying out of operations in furtherance of the common criminal plan. They were well trained for such persecutory operations. I refer the Chamber to the confidential evidence table at F9. Witness evidence is that Arkan's Tigers were operating in Sanski Most in co-ordination with the local TO. I refer the Chamber now to the confidential evidence table at F10. Arkan's Men were operating in the Sanski Most area at least between the 22nd of September and the 10th of October in conjunction with other Serb forces including police from Serbia, military police, and members of the VRS. Please refer to the confidential evidence table at F11. In P284, excerpted on slide 86, Arkan's own words provide additional evidence of his persecutory intent. I also refer the Chamber to P282 and P283. Financial support from the DB provided additional means for Arkan's Men to operate and in some cases even to recruit additional fighters. P289, appearing on slide 87, dated the 23rd of September, 1995, is a letter signed by Ratko Mladic reporting on the activities of Arkan and his men in Sanski Most. The document reads: "Members of the SDG paramilitary units forcibly induct into their ranks or recruit VRS members promising them a salary of 600 dinars, 10.000 dinars compensation if they are wounded, unemployment, and health insurance through the MUP of the Republic of Serbia." According to this document, Arkan was operating under the official approval of Radovan Karadzic while identifying himself as "a mountain brigade of the MUP of Serbia and RS." The SDG members were paid directly in freshly printed money by the DB, at times individual SDG members would go to the DB offices directly to pick up the money for salaries and at other times, the money would be sent in bags to the SDG office. The largest amount of payment by the DB to the SDG was reportedly received after the Banja Luka operations, including Sanski Most in September 1995. I refer the Chamber to P1616 and 1619 and to P440 and P441. The Prosecution has tendered into evidence in this case official DB payment records spanning at least from the end of 1993 onward into the postwar period. Listed on these payment records fully corroborating witness testimony are numerous known members of Arkan's Tigers, the SDG, whose monthly payments by the DB were officially recorded throughout the latter part of 1994 and through 1995, covering the time-period during which the Sanski Most crimes were committed. I refer the Chamber to the transcript at page 8886 and 7. On one DB payment record, which I request not to be broadcast to the public, please, P454, page 19, the first name on that list is Milorad Ulemek, aka Legija, and there are at least 15 SDG members officially documented as having been paid by the DB directly that month, including Mile, Mihajlo Ulemek and Jugoslav Gluscevic, combined on the same list with several SDB members who were paid simultaneously with the Tigers. I refer the Chamber to the confidential evidence table at F12 and to the transcript at page 8892 and 3. P454 is only one example. Next slide, also please not to be broadcast. It is the Prosecution's case that numerous payment records on which known SDG members and DB members are listed bear the signature of Franko Simatovic. The Prosecution refers the Chamber as additional examples to P456, P457, P458, and for corroboration to P1080. A former SDG member confirmed during his testimony that Rajo Bozovic received his payment from the same place that Arkan's Men did. This assertion is borne out on the payment records. I refer the Chamber to P465, a DB payment record that Bozovic and other DB members, as well as numerous SDG members are listed. This payment record is also signed by Franko Simatovic. One witness had was a former member of Arkan's SDG and who participated in the Pauk joint operation in Velika Kladusa gave evidence that Legija addressed Frenki "with the title, boss." P59 is a video of a parade in Bijeljina at which Karadzic thanks and congratulates Arkan and his SDG. This public display of praise and approval from the RS President Karadzic took place just following the attack on Sanski Most. The discriminatory intent is clear from both words and actions. The DB provided communication and ensured the reliability of the paths of communication between Frenki and Arkan as JCE members. The DB created a direct telephone line from the Erdut camp, which Arkan used as his base, as well as a direct radio link from Arkan's office in Belgrade to the Erdut camp. I refer the Chamber to P1615, 1616, and 1619. Arkan visited Frenki in his office for meetings frequently during the time from the end of 1994 into the summer of 1995. I refer the Chamber to P1619, P1615, and to the confidential evidence table at F13. For additional evidence corroborating Arkan's co-ordination with the DB, I refer the Chamber to the confidential evidence table at F14, and F15. P1192 is a report from a DB operative from Novi Sad regarding the activities of Arkan in the territory of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem where Arkan's Erdut training centre was located. The document explains that following the fall of the western part of the RSK in August 1995, the MUP of Serbia sent members of the SVK, who had fled the FRY to Arkan's training centre in Erdut. There, these members of the SVK were trained for five to ten days in Arkan's training centre and subsequently sent to the front line. The intelligence source reports that "Arkan is in" -- Your Honours, I'm conscious of the time, I have about five minutes left. I've truly tried to trim it back and Mr. Groome has three minutes. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I saw Mr. Groome is last on the list. What does that mean? Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That means that Mr. Groome will be delivering a few minutes of conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I need two minutes, really not more, for procedural matters. Ms. Marcus, you said five minutes, a couple of more minutes for Mr. Groome, I expect you to finish at 10 minutes to 2.00, if the interpreters and others assisting us would have no major problems with that. I don't hear yet of major problems, let's proceed as quickly as possible, not by speeding up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In this document, P1192, Arkan announced that his task was to "immediately establish peace, order and strict discipline among civilians. Two to three civilians are to be killed. That specifically applied to the village of Sodelovci, in order to cause fear among the people." Just as in Pauk and in Trnovo, in Sanski Most the Serbian MUP provided multiple licence plates and ensured movement across borders. A witness corroborated this, explaining that the MUP Serbian licence plates were authentic and issued by the MUP of Serbia to the SDG. I refer the Chamber to the confidential evidence table at F16. An example of the benefit of multiple licence plates and facilitation to cross borders occurred on the occasion of the filming of the video, P59, of the parade in Bijeljina. Prior to this event, a call was placed to the Serbian MUP on a direct emergency telephone line which had been provided to the SDG by the MUP authorities. That call to the Serbian MUP facilitated Arkan's movement across the border into Bosnia from Serbia across the Raca crossing. I refer the Chamber to the confidential evidence table at F17. Just as in Velika Kladusa, in Trnovo, and now in Sanski Most, the accused participated in the implementation of the common criminal plan and designed and ordered the crimes charged through the same pattern of mechanisms which as high level MUP officials in a JCE network they were uniquely placed to provide. Co-ordination and deployment; visits to the field, in person or via agents; ammunition and weapons; transportation buses from Serbia; training; ensuring border crossings; multiple licence plates; direct salary and per diem payments; a variety of uniforms; communication through radio and telephone; and other logistical support just as Milosevic said, Jovica will resolve the logistical problems. I will conclude with some excerpts from General Ratko Mladic's diary. First is Exhibit P2543, quoting General Gvero as saying, "The municipality of Sanski Most is controlled by many wearing Arkan's uniform." General Milovanovic at the same meeting is noted by Mladic as stating: "300 Arkan's volunteers arrived and were put into the RS MUP. They were reportedly meant to be behind the lines and arrest all those who are fleeing from the front." In an entry just a few days later, the 29th of September, 1995, Mladic records President Karadzic as saying: "Jovica Stanisic is angry about something. He gave 300 of his men and the US is begrudging us for having advertised Arkan." And finally in notes taken of a meeting involving General Perisic and the accused Jovica Stanisic on the 30th of September, 1995, General Mladic quotes Jovica Stanisic as saying: "Arkan is embedded there, we sent 400 people. As far as I have been informed, this helped at Sanski Most and Novi Grad." Your Honours, I will now turn the floor over to Mr. Groome. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, I had one observation that I believe will be equally appropriate in sur-rebuttal, so I will just say at this stage that this completes the Prosecution's submissions on each of the major areas of the indictment. It is the Prosecution's position that each individual body of evidence presented to you today, as sections C through F, individually establishes a basis upon which Mr. Simatovic's application should be denied. Taken together, the Prosecution has clearly met its burden at this stage of the proceedings. With that, Your Honour, we conclude our submissions. I would ask that the PowerPoint and table of confidential exhibits be assigned Exhibit numbers and marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Groome. I just asked Madam Registrar whether they had been uploaded, she had not received an answer to that yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, they will be uploaded as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I notice that of course the confidential, the table of confidential evidence should be marked for identification confidentially. How about the slides? Apart from 88 and 89, perhaps, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Right, those are the two, yes, Your Honour, those are the two that would have to be under seal, those two slides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but are you not -- do you want to have them marked for identification individually or are you uploading one series without 88 and 89 and then in addition to that, one consisting of 88 and 89?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That's a good suggestion, Your Honour. We will upload one version without those two slides and then as Your Honour sees fit -- that one can be public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then the two remaining slides in a separate --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Separate document, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you already perhaps preassign numbers. The first for the series of slides without slides 88 and 89.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be P2973, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would be public. Then slides 88 and 89 would receive number ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P2974, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then finally the table of references to confidential evidence would receive?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P2975, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would also be confidential, therefore under seal. One very quick question, the Simatovic Defence has filed a request for certification to appeal the Scheduling Order and a decision on Defence requests for adjustment of Scheduling Order of the 16th of February. Does the Stanisic Defence want to respond or to make submissions on that request?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And may I take it that the Prosecution wishes to do so?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could we have an expedited filing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: End of the week suit the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, end of the week would be then the time-limits on which we have agreed by now. Yes. Then, there being no other procedural matters on my agenda, we adjourn for the day and we'll resume and hear further submissions tomorrow, Tuesday, the 12th of April, quarter past 2.00 in this same Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 12th day of April, 2011 at 2.15 p.m.
